description: Talent pipeline index: research output quality (35%, OpenAlex), domestic PhD pipeline (25%, NSF/MoE), and elite researcher concentration + migration (40%, MacroPolo). See talent_manual.json for pipeline and migration data sources.

pipeline.confidence: High — government survey covering all US PhD-granting institutions

elite_migration.confidence: Medium-High — systematic methodology on public conference proceedings; lag of 1-2 years from latest venue; elite venue selection may not capture applied AI research
elite_migration.migration_note: China's domestic retention of China-origin top researchers has increased from ~25% (2019 cohort) to ~34% (2022 cohort). The US share has declined slightly but remains dominant.

pipeline.source: China Ministry of Education (MoE) Statistics 2022 / 教育部统计数据
pipeline.confidence: Medium — official statistics, but classification of 'AI-related' is broader than Western definitions; peer-reviewed verification limited
pipeline.coverage_note: China MoE 2022 reports ~52,000 CS/IT-category doctoral graduates. Estimated 30% are AI/ML-adjacent. China's broad CS classification includes applied software engineering that would not typically be classified as AI research in Western databases. Adjusted estimate is conservative. Note: a significant share of top Chinese AI researchers do their PhD in the US or Europe.

elite_migration.confidence: Medium-High — systematic methodology on public conference proceedings; lag of 1-2 years from latest venue; elite venue selection may not capture applied AI research
elite_migration.migration_note: China's domestic retention of China-origin top researchers has increased from ~25% (2019 cohort) to ~34% (2022 cohort). The US share has declined slightly but remains dominant.

openalex.methodology_note: Papers counted once per country where ≥1 author has an identified institution. Multinational papers counted in both countries — sums exceed total paper count. High-impact and top-cited queries add a cited_by_count filter which may not work on all OpenAlex instances (falls back to seeded estimates if the filter returns zero results). OpenAlex does not de-duplicate authors across papers; a prolific researcher counts once per paper, not once per researcher.

coverage_warning: Three measurement gaps affect all talent assessments: (1) Affiliation vs. origin — a China-born researcher working at MIT is counted under the US, inflating the US share in publication-based metrics; (2) Quality vs. quantity — China produces 3-5x the PhD volume but the US captures a disproportionate share of elite researchers at frontier labs; (3) Migration direction — the US has historically attracted China-born AI talent, but return migration to China has accelerated since ~2019.
